title: Classification of Rational $c=1$ Vertex Operator Algebras and Vertex Operator Superalgebras
abstract: For mathematicians: In this first in a series of two papers, we give a mathematically rigorous classification of (sufficiently nice) $c=1$ vertex operator algebras (VOAs) and vertex operator superalgebras (VOSAs). We confirm the lore that any such VO(S)A is either a lattice VO(S)A $V_L$ associated to a rank-1 integral lattice $L$, or can be obtained as an orbifold thereof, i.e. a $G$-invariant subalgebra $V_L^G$ for some finite group $G$ of automorphisms. All such $G$ are known, allowing for an explicit enumeration of nice $c=1$ VO(S)As. A key ingredient in our approach is to establish a general criterion for nice VOAs, requiring knowledge only of the vacuum character, for testing when the simple modules with integer conformal dimension span a symmetric fusion subcategory which is braided tensor equivalent to $Rep(G)$. In our companion paper, we calculate the ribbon auto-equivalences of the representation categories of the nice $c=1$ VOAs, and leverage this to obtain the classification of nice bosonic and fermionic $c=1$ full conformal field theories.   For physicists: We rigorously classify the chiral algebras that can arise in the holomorphic sector of a bosonic or fermionic rational $c=1$ conformal field theory (CFT) whose non-identity primaries all have positive conformal dimension. Thinking of chiral algebras as gapless boundary conditions of 3D topological quantum field theories (TQFTs), our result says that any such chiral algebra is either a holomorphic boundary of $U(1)_k$ Chern-Simons theory, or can be obtained by passing to the $G$-invariant states thereof for some finite group $G$ of symmetries. We explicitly enumerate these chiral algebras and also discuss their non-invertible symmetries. In a companion paper, we build on these results using techniques from the study of 3D TQFTs to classify full bosonic and fermionic rational $c=1$ CFTs.
summary: This paper rigorously classifies all 'nice' Vertex Operator Algebras and Superalgebras with central charge $c=1$. It proves that these algebras must arise either from rank-1 integral lattices or as orbifolds of such lattices. This classification has deep implications for understanding the chiral algebras that form the holomorphic sector of rational $c=1$ Conformal Field Theories.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide a mathematically rigorous classification of 'nice' $c=1$ Vertex Operator Algebras (VOAs) and Vertex Operator Superalgebras (VOSAs). Physically, this translates to classifying the chiral algebras arising in the holomorphic sector of rational $c=1$ Conformal Field Theories (CFTs).
main_result: The classification states that any such VOA must be isomorphic to a lattice VOA ($	ext{V}_L$) or an orbifold thereof ($	ext{V}_L^G$). The list includes specific examples like $	ext{V}_{2m}$ and three exceptional algebras ($	ext{V}T, 	ext{V}O, 	ext{V}I$).
method: The mathematical approach relies on showing that these VOAs are Tannakian, using criteria based on the vacuum character and the structure of simple modules. Physically, the classification is linked to viewing the VOA as the boundary theory of a 3D Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT).
model_or_system: The primary mathematical objects are $c=1$ VOAs/VOSAs. Physically, the context is the study of rational bosonic or fermionic CFTs, particularly those whose non-identity primaries have positive conformal dimension.
key_observables: The vacuum character ($	ext{ch}_V(	au)$) and the function $P_V(	au)$ (related to modules with integer conformal dimension) are key diagnostic tools.
important_parameters: The central charge $c=1$ is the defining parameter. The classification depends on the structure of the associated finite symmetry group $G$ and the lattice rank.
main_assumptions: The classification is restricted to 'nice' VOAs (strongly rational and pseudo-unitary). The full classification of CFTs is reserved for a companion paper.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the conformal moduli space of unitary 2D CFTs with $c=1$. Figure 2 illustrates the physical proof sequence: TQFT $	o$ Chern-Simons theory $	o$ VOA boundary.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the mathematical criterion for nice VOAs using the vacuum character, proving that they must be lattice VOAs or orbifolds. It then connects this structure to the physical realization as chiral algebras in $c=1$ CFTs, with the full classification of full CFTs deferred to a companion work.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, the rigorous classification of low-dimensional CFTs (like $c=1$) provides fundamental constraints on quantum field theories, which informs the understanding of boundary conditions and topological order relevant to quantum information.

Figure 2: A physical interpretation of our proof of the classification of nice c = 1 chiral algebras. We argue that any such chiral algebra V occurs on the boundary of a TQFT whose spinless anyons generate a Rep(G) one-form symmetry. When Rep(G) is gauged, the bulk goes over to U(1)2t⋆ Chern-Simons theory for some square-free t⋆, and the boundary goes over to the free chiral boson theory V2t⋆. Figure 3: The bulk TQFT supporting V¯0 on its boundary is assumed to have a fermionic anyon f. The boundary local operators on which it terminates belong to the Hilbert space V¯1. Fermionizing entails stacking with sVec, which has a transparent fermion ψ, and gauging the Z2 one-form symmetry generated by f ⊗ψ. The bulk after fermionizing is a spin TQFT, and the boundary is a fermionic chiral algebra V ∼= V¯0 ⊕V¯1. The fermionized theory has a fermion parity zero-form symmetry denoted (−1)F. Fermionization can be undone by bosonization, which entails gauging (−1)F. The effect on the boundary is to project out the operators which are odd under (−1)F.
